tagline: The whole Oregon shore on 101, from Astoria to the redwoods.
intro: Out of Astoria, at the northwest tip of the state, US 101 runs south through Seaside and Cannon Beach and climbs to 700 feet above the Pacific past Neahkahnie Mountain, the highest the road gets over the sea. Then it drifts inland to the dairy country at Tillamook and comes back to the shore at Lincoln City.

Past Newport, Yachats and Florence the cliffs give way to sand, then to the harbors of Coos Bay and Bandon, the mouth of the Rogue at Gold Beach and finally Brookings, five miles short of the California redwoods. Nine lighthouses stand along the way.
season: Winter and spring for whale watching, summer and fall for the weather.

moments.title: Haystack Rock
moments.text: A 235-foot basalt stack, reachable on foot at low tide. In July 2023 it was closed for a spell after a cougar was found climbing it in search of prey.

moments.title: Cape Perpetua
moments.text: Captain Cook named it on St. Perpetua's Day, 1778. From the 800-foot crest the coast shows for 70 miles, and by the shore lie great heaps of mussel shells the Alsea left behind.

moments.title: Oregon Dunes
moments.text: Some forty miles of sand between Florence and Coos Bay, a few dunes 500 feet high. Frank Herbert's research on them helped inspire the novel Dune.
